u2-l1.0.note.en: To a stranger, a teacher or a group: **Odkiaľ ste?**
u2-l1.0.note.t: Notanish odamga, oʻqituvchiga yoki guruhga: **Odkiaľ ste?**

u2-l1.1.note.en: Írsko = Ireland. After **z** (from), the -o at the end changes to **-a**: z Írsk**a**.
u2-l1.1.note.t: Írsko = Irlandiya. **z** = «-dan». Oʻzbekchada qoʻshimcha soʻz oxiriga qoʻshiladi, slovakchada esa **z** soʻz oldiga qoʻyiladi (bu predlog). Bunda oxirdagi -o **-a** boʻladi: z Írsk**a** = Irlandiyadan.

u2-l1.3.note.en: **je** = is. Before s, z, š or ž, “z” becomes **zo**: zo Slovenska.
u2-l1.3.note.t: **je** = «-dir» (u … boʻladi). Oʻzbekchada u koʻpincha tushib qoladi, slovakchada esa kerak. s, z, š yoki ž oldidan «z» **zo** boʻladi: zo Slovenska.

u2-l1.4.note.en: Many country names end in -sko or -cko. From Germany: z Nemecka.
u2-l1.4.note.t: Koʻp davlat nomlari -sko yoki -cko bilan tugaydi. Germaniyadan: z Nemecka.

u2-l1.6.why.en: “From” is **zo** before s, z, š or ž, and Slovensko starts with s. Elsewhere it's just z: z Írska, z Nemecka.
u2-l1.6.why.t: «…dan» maʼnosidagi z soʻzi s, z, š yoki ž oldidan **zo** boʻladi, Slovensko esa s bilan boshlanadi. Boshqa hollarda shunchaki z: z Írska, z Nemecka.

en: After z (from), the -o at the end changes to **-a**: Nemecko → z Nemeck**a**.
Nemecko starts with n, so “from” is plain **z**. Zo is only for words starting with s, z, š or ž: zo Slovenska.
t: z («-dan») soʻzidan keyin oxirdagi -o **-a** ga aylanadi: Nemecko → z Nemeck**a** (Germaniyadan).
Nemecko n bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun «-dan» — oddiy **z**. Zo faqat s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻzlar oldidan keladi: zo Slovenska.

u2-l1.8.note.en: Most countries ending in -a change it to **-y**: Ukrajin**a** → z Ukrajin**y**, Amerik**a** → z Amerik**y**.
u2-l1.8.note.t: -a bilan tugaydigan koʻp davlat nomlarida u **-y** boʻladi: Ukrajin**a** → z Ukrajin**y**, Amerik**a** → z Amerik**y**.

u2-l1.9.question.en: Peter is from America. Which sentence is right?

u2-l1.9.why.en: After z, Amerika changes -a to **-y**: z Amerik**y**. And it stays z: zo is only for words starting with s, z, š or ž.
u2-l1.9.why.t: z (…dan) soʻzidan keyin Amerika oxiridagi -a **-y** ga aylanadi: z Amerik**y**. zo esa faqat s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻzlardan oldin keladi.

u2-l1.10.en.en: Where are you from? I'm from Poland.

u2-l1.11.note.en: Nationalities have a form for men and one for women: Ír → Ír**ka**.
u2-l1.11.note.t: Millatlarning erkaklar va ayollar uchun alohida shakli bor: Ír → Ír**ka**. Oʻzbek tilida bunday farq yoʻq.

u2-l1.12.en.en: a Slovak man, a Slovak woman

u2-l1.12.note.en: Women's forms end in **-ka**: Sloven**ka**, Nem**ka** (German), Talian**ka** (Italian). Men's: Slovák, Nemec, Talian.
u2-l1.12.note.t: Ayollar shakli **-ka** bilan tugaydi: Sloven**ka**, Nem**ka** (nemis), Talian**ka** (italyan). Erkaklar shakli: Slovák, Nemec, Talian.

u2-l1.14.why.en: Emma is a woman, so she takes the women's form with **-ka**: Ír**ka**. Ír is for a man.
u2-l1.14.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun **-ka** bilan ayol shakli keladi: Ír**ka**. Ír esa erkak uchun (oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham «irlandiyalik»).

u2-l1.15.why.en: **Slovenka** is the women's form, so it's a Slovak woman: Lucia. Tomáš would say Som Slovák, and Emma is Irish: Som Írka.
u2-l1.15.why.t: **Slovenka** — ayol shakli, demak bu slovak ayol, yaʼni Lusiya. Tomash Som Slovák derdi, Emma esa irlandiyalik: Som Írka.

en: Lucia is Slovak. She is from Slovakia.
**Byť** (to be) is irregular, like English am, are, is. Learn each form together with its pronoun.
The verb form already shows who it is, so the pronoun is often dropped: **Som** Emma. = I'm Emma.
t: **Byť** (boʻlmoq) — notoʻgʻri feʼl: shakllari qoidaga boʻysunmaydi. U oʻzbekchadagi -man, -san, -dir qoʻshimchalari oʻrnida keladi. Har bir shaklni olmoshi bilan birga yodlang.
Feʼl shaklining oʻzi kim haqida gap ketayotganini koʻrsatadi, shuning uchun olmosh koʻpincha tushib qoladi: **Som** Emma. = Emmaman.

u2-l2.1.title.en: Ty or vy? Oni or ony?
u2-l2.1.title.t: Ty yoki vy? Oni yoki ony?

en: **Ty**: one friend, a child, family. **Vy**: a stranger or a teacher (polite), or any group of people.
**Oni** = they, when there is at least one man in the group. **Ony** = they, for women only (or things).
t: **Ty**: bitta doʻst, bola, oila aʼzosi. **Vy**: notanish odam yoki oʻqituvchi (hurmat bilan) yoki har qanday guruh. Xuddi «sen» va «siz» kabi.
**Oni** = ular, agar guruhda kamida bitta erkak boʻlsa. **Ony** = ular, faqat ayollar (yoki narsalar) haqida. Oʻzbek tilida bu farq yoʻq: ikkalasi ham «ular».

en: Tomáš and Marek? They're from Slovakia.
Anna and Eva? They're from Poland.

u2-l2.2.why.en: With **ja** (I), byť is **som**. Si goes with ty, je with on or ona.
u2-l2.2.why.t: **ja** (men) bilan byť — **som**, oʻzbekchadagi -man kabi. Si ty bilan, je esa on yoki ona bilan keladi.

u2-l2.4.why.en: With **ty** (you, a friend), byť is **si**. Som goes with ja, ste with vy.
u2-l2.4.why.t: **ty** (sen, doʻstga) bilan byť — **si**, oʻzbekchadagi -san kabi: slovakmisan? Som ja bilan, ste esa vy bilan keladi.

u2-l2.5.question.en: You ask your teacher, pani Horváthová, where she is from. What do you say?
u2-l2.5.question.t: Oʻqituvchingiz Horvatova xonimdan qayerdan ekanini soʻramoqchisiz. Nima deysiz?

u2-l2.5.why.en: A teacher gets the polite **vy**, and with vy byť is **ste**. Odkiaľ si? is for a friend (ty); sú is for oni (they).
u2-l2.5.why.t: Oʻqituvchiga hurmat bilan **vy** (siz) deyiladi, vy bilan esa byť — **ste**. Odkiaľ si? — doʻstga (ty), sú esa oni (ular) uchun.

en: We is **my**, and with my byť is **sme**. Ste goes with vy (you).
Slovensko starts with s, and before s, z, š or ž, “from” is **zo**. Plain z is for the rest: z Írska.
t: «Biz» — **my**, my bilan esa byť — **sme**, oʻzbekchadagi -miz kabi. Ste esa vy (siz) bilan keladi.
Slovensko s bilan boshlanadi, s, z, š yoki ž oldidan esa «-dan» — **zo**. Boshqa hollarda oddiy z keladi: z Írska.

u2-l2.7.en.en: Tomáš and Lucia are from Slovakia.

u2-l2.7.why.en: Tomáš and Lucia are two people, **oni** (they), and with oni byť is **sú**. Je is for one person, sme for my (we).
u2-l2.7.why.t: Tomash va Lusiya — ikki kishi, **oni** (ular), oni bilan esa byť — **sú**. Je — bitta kishi uchun, sme — my (biz) uchun.

u2-l2.9.question.en: Anna and Eva: which word means “they”?
u2-l2.9.question.t: Anna va Eva: qaysi soʻz «ular» degani?

u2-l2.9.why.en: **Ony** is “they” for women only, like Anna and Eva. **Oni** needs at least one man in the group, and ono means “it”.
u2-l2.9.why.t: **Ony** — faqat ayollar haqida «ular», Anna va Eva kabi. **Oni** uchun guruhda kamida bitta erkak boʻlishi kerak, ono esa bitta narsa haqida «u».

u2-l2.10.prompt.en: Are you Slovak? (to a male friend)

en: A friend gets **ty**, and with ty byť is **si**. Ste is for vy: a stranger, a teacher or a group.
Your friend is a man, so it's **Slovák**. Slovenka, with -ka, is a Slovak woman.
t: Doʻstga **ty** (sen) deyiladi, ty bilan esa byť — **si**, oʻzbekchadagi -san kabi. Ste — vy uchun: notanish odam, oʻqituvchi yoki guruh.
Doʻstingiz — erkak, shuning uchun **Slovák**. -ka bilan Slovenka esa slovak ayol.

u2-l2.11.en.en: Excuse me, are you from Germany?

u2-l2.11.why.en: Prepáčte already shows the polite **vy**, and with vy byť is **ste**. Si goes with ty, sú with oni.
u2-l2.11.why.t: Prepáčte (kechirasiz) hurmatli **vy** ekanini koʻrsatadi, vy bilan esa byť — **ste**, oʻzbekchadagi -siz kabi. Si ty bilan, sú esa oni bilan keladi.

en: Most words for people have a masculine and a feminine form. The feminine one often adds **-ka**.
Slovak has no word for “a” or “the”: Lucia je študentka. = Lucia is a student.
t: Odamlarni bildiradigan koʻp soʻzlarning erkak va ayol shakli bor. Ayol shakli koʻpincha **-ka** qoʻshib yasaladi. Oʻzbek tilida bunday farq yoʻq: «talaba» ikkalasi uchun ham.
**je** soʻzini tushirib qoldirmang: Lucia je študentka. = Lusiya talaba.

u2-l3.1.why.en: Lucia is a woman, so she takes the feminine form with **-ka**: študent**ka**. Študent is for a man.
u2-l3.1.why.t: Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun **-ka** bilan ayol shakli keladi: študent**ka**. Študent esa erkak uchun (oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham «talaba»).

en: Jana is a woman, so she takes the feminine form with **-ka**: učiteľ**ka**. Učiteľ is for a man.
Jana is **ona** (she), and with ona byť is **je**. Som goes with ja (I).
t: Yana — ayol, shuning uchun **-ka** bilan ayol shakli keladi: učiteľ**ka**. Učiteľ esa erkak uchun.
Yana haqida «u» — **ona**, ona bilan esa byť — **je**. Som ja (men) bilan keladi.

u2-l3.3.question.en: Which word means a female friend?

u2-l3.3.why.en: The feminine form adds **-ka**: kamarát → kamarát**ka**. Učiteľka is feminine too, but it means a female teacher.
u2-l3.3.why.t: Ayol shakli **-ka** qoʻshib yasaladi: kamarát → kamarát**ka**. Učiteľka ham ayol shakli, lekin u «oʻqituvchi (ayol)» degani.

u2-l3.4.en.en: Peter is German, and Anna is German too.

u2-l3.4.why.en: Peter is a man, so he takes the masculine form: **Nemec**. Nemka is for a woman, and Nemecko is the country, Germany.
u2-l3.4.why.t: Peter — erkak, shuning uchun erkak shakli keladi: **Nemec**. Nemka — ayol uchun, Nemecko esa mamlakat, Germaniya.

en: Every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter. The last letter usually tells you which: a consonant means masculine, **-a** feminine, **-o** or **-e** neuter.
Watch out for exceptions: dievč**a** (girl) is neuter, and noc (night) is feminine.
t: Slovak tilida har bir ot erkak, ayol yoki oʻrta jinsda boʻladi. Bu grammatik qoida, oʻzbek tilida u yoʻq, shuning uchun soʻzni jinsi bilan birga yodlang. Odatda oxirgi harf yordam beradi: undosh — erkak jinsi, **-a** — ayol jinsi, **-o** yoki **-e** — oʻrta jins.
Istisnolar ham bor: dievč**a** (qiz bola) — oʻrta jins, noc (tun) esa ayol jinsi.

u2-l3.7.why.en: Nouns ending in **-a** are usually feminine: izb**a**. Internát ends in a consonant (masculine), and auto in -o (neuter).
u2-l3.7.why.t: **-a** bilan tugaydigan otlar odatda ayol jinsida boʻladi: izb**a**. Internát undosh bilan tugaydi (erkak jinsi), auto esa -o bilan (oʻrta jins).

u2-l3.8.why.en: **Dievča** (girl) is an exception: it ends in -a but is neuter. Žena is feminine, and muž, ending in a consonant, is masculine.
u2-l3.8.why.t: **Dievča** (qiz bola) — istisno: -a bilan tugasa ham, oʻrta jinsda. Žena — ayol jinsi, undosh bilan tugaydigan muž esa erkak jinsi.

u2-l3.9.why.en: Lucia is a woman, so “she” is **ona**. On is he, ono is it.
u2-l3.9.why.t: Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun «u» — **ona**. On erkak haqida, ono esa oʻrta jinsdagi soʻz haqida aytiladi. Oʻzbekchada uchalasi ham «u».

u2-l3.10.why.en: Peter is a man, so “he” is **on**. Ona is she, ono is it.
u2-l3.10.why.t: Peter — erkak, shuning uchun «u» — **on**. Ona ayol haqida, ono esa oʻrta jinsdagi soʻz haqida aytiladi.

u2-l3.12.prompt.en: Martin is a teacher and Eva is a student.

en: Martin is a man, so he takes the masculine form: **učiteľ**. Učiteľka, with -ka, is for a woman.
Eva is a woman, so she takes the feminine form with **-ka**: študent**ka**. Študent is for a man.
t: Martin — erkak, shuning uchun erkak shakli keladi: **učiteľ**. -ka bilan učiteľka esa ayol uchun.
Eva — ayol, shuning uchun **-ka** bilan ayol shakli keladi: študent**ka**. Študent esa erkak uchun (oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham «talaba»).

u2-l4.0.title.en: Verbs: an ending for each person
u2-l4.0.title.t: Feʼllar: har bir shaxsga oʻz qoʻshimchasi

en: Slovak verbs change their ending to show who is doing something: **-m** (I), **-š** (you), no ending (he, she), **-me** (we), **-te** (you), and **-jú**, **-ú** or **-ia** (they).
Like hovoriť: **robiť** (to do) → robím, robíš, robí… Čo robíš? = What do you do?
Languages go with **po**: hovoriť po slovensky (Slovak), po anglicky (English), po nemecky (German).
t: Slovak feʼllari ham, oʻzbek feʼllari kabi, kim bajarayotganini qoʻshimcha bilan koʻrsatadi: **-m** (men), **-š** (sen), qoʻshimchasiz (u), **-me** (biz), **-te** (siz) va **-jú**, **-ú** yoki **-ia** (ular). Solishtiring: hovorí**m** — gapiraman.
Xuddi hovoriť kabi: **robiť** (qilmoq) → robím, robíš, robí… Čo robíš? = Nima ish qilasan?
Tillar **po** bilan aytiladi: hovoriť po slovensky (slovakcha gapirmoq), po anglicky (inglizcha), po nemecky (nemischa).

u2-l4.1.why.en: With on or ona, the verb has no ending: Lucia **hovorí**. Hovorím (-m) is ja, hovoria (-ia) is oni.
u2-l4.1.why.t: on yoki ona bilan feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: Lucia **hovorí**. Hovorím (-m) — ja, hovoria (-ia) — oni shakli.

u2-l4.2.why.en: Tomáš and Marek are **oni** (they), so hovoriť ends in **-ia**: hovor**ia**. Hovorí is one person, hovoríme is my (we).
u2-l4.2.why.t: Tomash va Marek — **oni** (ular), shuning uchun hovoriť **-ia** bilan tugaydi: hovor**ia**. Hovorí — bitta kishi, hovoríme — my (biz) shakli.

en: “Her” name means **ona**, and with on or ona the verb has no ending: Ako sa **volá**? Voláš is ty (you).
“Her” name means **ona**, and with on or ona the verb has no ending: Ako sa **volá**? Volám is ja (I).
t: «Uning ismi» haqida soʻralyapti, yaʼni on yoki ona haqida, ular bilan esa feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: Ako sa **volá**? Voláš — ty (sen) shakli.
«Uning ismi» haqida soʻralyapti, yaʼni on yoki ona haqida, ular bilan esa feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: Ako sa **volá**? Volám — ja (men) shakli.

u2-l4.4.question.en: How do you say “We speak Slovak”?

u2-l4.4.why.en: With **my** (we), the verb ends in **-me**: hovorí**me**. -te is for vy, -ia for oni (they).
u2-l4.4.why.t: **my** (biz) bilan feʼl **-me** bilan tugaydi: hovorí**me**, oʻzbekchadagi -miz kabi (gapiramiz). -te — vy uchun, -ia — oni (ular) uchun.

en: Verbs in **-ovať** change -ova- to **-uje-**: študovať → študujem. **Pracovať** (to work) does the same: pracujem.
Verbs in **-ieť** keep -ie-: rozumieť → rozumiem. Only “they” is different: rozume**jú**.
t: **-ovať** bilan tugaydigan feʼllarda -ova- **-uje-** boʻladi: študovať → študujem. **Pracovať** (ishlamoq) ham shunday: pracujem.
**-ieť** bilan tugaydigan feʼllarda -ie- saqlanadi: rozumieť → rozumiem. Faqat «ular» shakli boshqacha: rozume**jú**.

en: Do you understand? — Yes, I do.

u2-l4.7.why.en: Marek is **on**, so the verb has no ending, just like študuje: **pracuje**. Pracujem is ja, pracujú is oni.
u2-l4.7.why.t: Marek — **on**, shuning uchun feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi, xuddi študuje kabi: **pracuje**. Pracujem — ja, pracujú — oni shakli.

u2-l4.8.why.en: Lucia and Tomáš are **oni**, and the “they” form of rozumieť is the different one: rozume**jú**. Rozumie is one person, rozumieme is my.
u2-l4.8.why.t: Lusiya va Tomash — **oni**, rozumieť feʼlining «ular» shakli esa boshqacha: rozume**jú**. Rozumie — bitta kishi, rozumieme — my shakli.

u2-l4.9.prompt.en: Tomáš, do you work as a programmer?

en: You're asking Tomáš himself, **ty**, so the verb ends in **-š**: pracuje**š**. Pracuje is for on or ona.
You're asking Tomáš himself, **ty**, so the verb ends in **-š**: pracuje**š**. Pracujem, with -m, is ja (I).
t: Siz Tomashning oʻzidan soʻrayapsiz, yaʼni **ty** (sen), shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: pracuje**š**, oʻzbekchadagi -san kabi. Pracuje — on yoki ona uchun.
Siz Tomashning oʻzidan soʻrayapsiz, yaʼni **ty** (sen), shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: pracuje**š**. -m bilan pracujem — ja (men) shakli.

u2-l4.12.en.en: What do you do? — I study.

u2-l4.12.why.en: The answer študujem is ja, so the question asks **ty** (you), and the verb ends in **-š**: robí**š**. Robím is ja, robia is oni.
u2-l4.12.why.t: Javobdagi študujem — ja shakli, demak savolda **ty** (sen) shakli keladi va feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: robí**š**. Robím — ja, robia — oni.

en: To say “not”, put **ne-** in front of the verb. It is written as one word.
A phrase to know by heart: **Ne**rozumiem. = I don't understand.
t: Inkor uchun feʼl oldiga **ne-** qoʻyiladi va qoʻshib yoziladi. Oʻzbekchada esa «-ma» feʼlning ichiga qoʻshiladi: gapiraman → gapirmayman.
Yod olish kerak boʻlgan ibora: **Ne**rozumiem. = Tushunmayapman.

u2-l5.1.why.en: **Ne-** goes in front, and the ending still shows the person: Marek is on, so **nehovorí**. Nehovorím is ja, nehovoria is oni.
u2-l5.1.why.t: **Ne-** feʼl oldiga qoʻshiladi, qoʻshimcha esa baribir shaxsni koʻrsatadi: Marek — on, demak **nehovorí**. Nehovorím — ja, nehovoria — oni.

u2-l5.2.why.en: **Ne-** goes in front of the verb, written as one word: **ne**študujem. Only byť takes a separate **nie**: nie som.
u2-l5.2.why.t: **Ne-** feʼl oldiga qoʻshib yoziladi: **ne**študujem, xuddi oʻzbekchadagi -ma- kabi (oʻqimayman). Alohida **nie** faqat byť bilan keladi: nie som.

en: We is **my**, so the verb ends in **-me**: nehovorí**me**. Nehovoríte, with -te, is vy.
To say “not”, put **ne-** in front of the verb, written as one word: **ne**hovoríme. Only byť takes a separate nie: nie som.
t: «Biz» — **my**, shuning uchun feʼl **-me** bilan tugaydi: nehovorí**me**, oʻzbekchadagi -miz kabi. -te bilan nehovoríte — vy shakli.
Inkor uchun feʼl oldiga **ne-** qoʻyiladi va qoʻshib yoziladi: **ne**hovoríme (gapirmaymiz). Alohida nie faqat byť bilan keladi: nie som.

u2-l5.5.question.en: Pán Kováč speaks very fast and you don't understand. What do you say?
u2-l5.5.question.t: Janob Kovach juda tez gapiryapti, siz esa tushunmayapsiz. Nima deysiz?

u2-l5.5.why.en: **Nerozumiem** is ne- + rozumiem, I don't understand, and pán Kováč gets the polite Prepáčte. Áno, rozumiem says the opposite; Nech sa páči is for handing something over.
u2-l5.5.why.t: **Nerozumiem** — ne- + rozumiem, «tushunmayapman», janob Kovachga esa hurmatli Prepáčte aytiladi. Áno, rozumiem buning teskarisi, Nech sa páči esa biror narsa uzatganda aytiladi.

en: **Byť** is the exception. It takes a separate word, **nie**, in front of the verb.
When you answer “no”, you often hear nie twice: Si Slovák? — **Nie, nie** som.
t: **Byť** — istisno. Uning oldiga alohida **nie** soʻzi qoʻyiladi. Bu oʻzbekchadagi «emas»ga oʻxshaydi: **nie som** = emasman.
«Yoʻq» deb javob berganda nie koʻpincha ikki marta eshitiladi: Si Slovák? — **Nie, nie** som. (Yoʻq, emasman.)

u2-l5.7.why.en: Byť takes a separate **nie**, and Emma is ona, so **nie je**. Nie si is ty, nie sú is oni.
u2-l5.7.why.t: Byť bilan alohida **nie** keladi, Emma esa ona, demak **nie je** (emas). Nie si — ty, nie sú — oni shakli.

u2-l5.8.question.en: “Si zo Slovenska?” You are from Ireland. What do you answer?
u2-l5.8.question.t: «Si zo Slovenska?» Siz Irlandiyadansiz. Nima deb javob berasiz?

u2-l5.8.why.en: You're not from Slovakia, and you answer as ja, so **nie som**. Nie si would mean “you aren't”.
u2-l5.8.why.t: Siz Slovakiyadan emassiz va oʻzingiz (ja) haqingizda javob berasiz, shuning uchun **nie som** (emasman). Nie si «sen emassan» degani boʻlardi.

en: Tomáš is a man, so he takes the masculine form: **Nemec**. Nemka is a German woman.
Tomáš is **on** (he), and with on byť is **je**: nie je, je Slovák. Som goes with ja (I).
t: Tomash — erkak, shuning uchun erkak shakli keladi: **Nemec**. Nemka esa nemis ayol.
Tomash — **on** (u), on bilan esa byť — **je**: nie je, je Slovák. Som ja (men) bilan keladi.

u2-l5.10.en.en: Lucia and Tomáš aren't from Ireland.

u2-l5.10.why.en: Lucia and Tomáš are **oni**, so byť is sú, with a separate nie: **nie sú**. Nie sme is my (we), nie ste is vy.
u2-l5.10.why.t: Lusiya va Tomash — **oni**, demak byť — sú, oldida alohida nie bilan: **nie sú**. Nie sme — my (biz), nie ste — vy shakli.

u2-l5.13.why.en: With **ja**, the verb ends in **-m**, and ne- goes in front: **nerozumiem**. Nerozumie is on or ona, nerozumejú is oni.
u2-l5.13.why.t: **ja** bilan feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi, ne- esa oldiga qoʻshiladi: **nerozumiem**. Nerozumie — on yoki ona, nerozumejú — oni shakli.

u2-l6.0.note.en: Zero is **nula**. “One” matches the noun's gender: jeden mobil, jedn**a** izba, jedn**o** auto.
u2-l6.0.note.t: Nol — **nula**. «Bir» soʻzi otning jinsiga moslashadi: jeden mobil (erkak jinsi), jedn**a** izba (ayol jinsi), jedn**o** auto (oʻrta jins).

u2-l6.5.en.t: oʻn bir, oʻn ikki, oʻn uch

u2-l6.5.note.en: 11–19 end in **-násť**: **štr**násť (14, a short form of štyri), pätnásť, šestnásť, sedemnásť, osemnásť, devätnásť.
u2-l6.5.note.t: 11–19 **-násť** bilan tugaydi: **štr**násť (14, štyri soʻzining qisqa shakli), pätnásť, šestnásť, sedemnásť, osemnásť, devätnásť.

u2-l6.6.note.en: From 50 on, tens end in **-desiat**: päťdesiat, šesťdesiat, sedemdesiat… And 100 is **sto**.
u2-l6.6.note.t: Ellikdan boshlab oʻnliklar **-desiat** bilan tugaydi: päťdesiat, šesťdesiat, sedemdesiat… 100 esa **sto**.

u2-l6.8.why.en: 11–19 end in **-násť**, and 14 uses the short form štr-: **štrnásť**. Štyri is 4, štyridsať is 40.
u2-l6.8.why.t: 11–19 **-násť** bilan tugaydi, 14 esa qisqa štr- shakli bilan yasaladi (štyri soʻzidan): **štrnásť**. Štyri — 4, štyridsať — 40.

u2-l6.9.note.en: Literally “How many years do you have?” Polite form: Koľko **máte** rokov?
u2-l6.9.note.t: Soʻzma-soʻz: «Nechta yiling bor?» Hurmat shakli: Koľko **máte** rokov?

u2-l6.10.note.en: **Mám** = I have (má = he or she has). Tens and ones join into one word: dvadsať + päť = **dvadsaťpäť**.
u2-l6.10.note.t: **Mám** = menda bor (má = unda bor). Oʻnliklar va birliklar bitta soʻz qilib yoziladi: dvadsať + päť = **dvadsaťpäť**.

en: Slovak gives your age with **mám** (I have), literally “I have twenty years”. Som means “I am”.
With dvadsať, “years” is **rokov**, just as in Mám dvadsaťpäť rokov and Koľko máš rokov?
t: Oʻzbekchada «yigirma yoshdaman» deymiz, slovakchada esa yosh **mám** («menda bor») bilan aytiladi: soʻzma-soʻz «yigirma yilim bor». Som bu yerda ishlatilmaydi.
dvadsať bilan «yil» — **rokov**, xuddi Mám dvadsaťpäť rokov va Koľko máš rokov? iboralaridagi kabi.

u2-l6.12.en.en: How old are you, Mr Kováč?

u2-l6.12.why.en: Pán Kováč gets the polite **vy**, so the verb ends in **-te**: má**te**. Máš is for a friend (ty).
u2-l6.12.why.t: Janob Kovachga hurmat bilan **vy** (siz) deyiladi, shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: má**te**. Máš — doʻstga (ty).

u2-l6.14.note.en: Words for order end in **-ý** or **-í**: prvý, druhý, tretí, štvrtý, piaty.
u2-l6.14.note.t: Tartib sonlar (oʻzbekchadagi -inchi kabi) **-ý** yoki **-í** bilan tugaydi: prvý, druhý, tretí, štvrtý, piaty.

u2-l6.15.why.en: Words for order end in **-ý** or **-í**, so **druhý** is second, like prvý (first). Two is dva.
u2-l6.15.why.t: Tartibni bildiruvchi soʻzlar **-ý** yoki **-í** bilan tugaydi, shuning uchun **druhý** — «ikkinchi», xuddi prvý (birinchi) kabi. «Ikki» esa dva.

u2-l6.16.why.en: “One” matches the noun's gender. Auto ends in -o, so it's neuter: **jedno**. Jeden is masculine (jeden mobil), jedna feminine (jedna izba).
u2-l6.16.why.t: «Bir» soʻzi otning jinsiga moslashadi. Auto -o bilan tugaydi, demak oʻrta jinsda: **jedno**. Jeden — erkak jinsi (jeden mobil), jedna — ayol jinsi (jedna izba).

u2-l7.0.en.en: Where are you from? I'm from Italy.

u2-l7.1.why.en: Slovensko starts with s, and before s, z, š or ž, “from” is **zo**. Other countries take z: z Írska.
u2-l7.1.why.t: Slovensko s bilan boshlanadi, s, z, š yoki ž oldidan esa «…dan» — **zo**. Boshqa mamlakatlar bilan z keladi: z Írska.

en: After z (from), the -o at the end changes to **-a**: Nemecko → z Nemeck**a**.
With **oni** (they), byť is **sú**. Sme goes with my (we).
t: z («-dan») soʻzidan keyin oxirdagi -o **-a** ga aylanadi: Nemecko → z Nemeck**a** (Germaniyadan).
«Ular» — **oni**, oni bilan esa byť — **sú**. Sme my (biz) bilan keladi.

u2-l7.3.en.en: I'm not a student, I'm a teacher.

u2-l7.3.why.en: Byť takes a separate **nie**, and ja goes with som: **nie som**. Nie je is on or ona, and plain som would mean “I am”.
u2-l7.3.why.t: Byť bilan alohida **nie** keladi, ja esa som bilan: **nie som** (emasman). Nie je — on yoki ona shakli. nie boʻlmasa, som študentka «talabaman» degani boʻlardi.

u2-l7.5.why.en: A noun ending in a consonant is usually masculine: **internát**. Univerzita ends in -a (feminine), mesto in -o (neuter).
u2-l7.5.why.t: Undosh bilan tugaydigan ot odatda erkak jinsida boʻladi: **internát**. Univerzita -a bilan tugaydi (ayol jinsi), mesto esa -o bilan (oʻrta jins).

u2-l7.6.why.en: Marek is **on**, so the verb has no ending: **pracuje**. Pracujem is ja, pracujú is oni.
u2-l7.6.why.t: Marek — **on**, shuning uchun feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: **pracuje**. Pracujem — ja, pracujú — oni shakli.

u2-l7.8.why.en: With **vy**, the verb ends in **-te**, just like pracujete: študuje**te**. Študuješ is ty, študujú is oni.
u2-l7.8.why.t: **vy** bilan feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi, xuddi pracujete kabi: študuje**te**. Študuješ — ty, študujú — oni shakli.

u2-l7.10.why.en: Twenty, thirty and forty end in **-dsať**: dvadsať, tridsať, štyri**dsať**. **-násť** is for 11–19: štrnásť is 14.
u2-l7.10.why.t: Yigirma, oʻttiz va qirq **-dsať** bilan tugaydi: dvadsať, tridsať, štyri**dsať**. **-násť** esa 11–19 uchun: štrnásť — 14.

u2-l7.11.prompt.en: I'm not from Slovakia. I'm from Ireland.

en: After z (from), the -o at the end changes to **-a**: Írsko → z Írsk**a**.
You're talking about yourself, **ja**, so byť is **som**: nie som, som z Írska. Je is for on or ona.
t: z («-dan») soʻzidan keyin oxirdagi -o **-a** ga aylanadi: Írsko → z Írsk**a** (Irlandiyadan).
Siz oʻzingiz haqingizda gapiryapsiz (ja), shuning uchun byť — **som**, oʻzbekchadagi -man kabi: nie som, som z Írska. Je — on yoki ona uchun.

u2-l7.12.question.en: You meet a new teacher for the first time. How do you ask her name?
u2-l7.12.question.t: Yangi oʻqituvchingiz (ayol) bilan ilk bor uchrashdingiz. Uning ismini qanday soʻraysiz?

u2-l7.12.why.en: A new teacher gets the polite **vy**, so the verb ends in **-te**: volá**te**. Voláš is for a friend (ty); volá is “he or she is called”.
u2-l7.12.why.t: Yangi oʻqituvchiga hurmat bilan **vy** (siz) deyiladi, shuning uchun feʼl **-te** bilan tugaydi: volá**te**. Voláš — doʻstga (ty), volá esa «uning ismi …» degani.

u2-l7.13.en.en: What are their names? — Tomáš and Marek.
u2-l7.13.en.t: Ularning ismi nima? — Tomash va Marek.

u2-l7.13.why.en: The answer names two people, **oni**, so the verb ends in **-jú**: vola**jú**. Voláme is my (we), volá is one person.
u2-l7.13.why.t: Javobda ikki kishi aytilgan, yaʼni **oni**, shuning uchun feʼl **-jú** bilan tugaydi: vola**jú**. Voláme — my (biz), volá — bitta kishi uchun.
